title: Muse Ember scores 36 on a public index, at about $0.14 a task
friendlyTitle: Meta's small model scores 36, at about 14 cents a task
summary: Meta released Muse Ember on 9 November for the steps agents repeat: tool calls, small coding jobs, routing, extraction, and long documents. On the Meta Model API it is muse-ember-1.0, at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, with a 1 million token window. Meta says its best setting scores 36 on the Artificial Analysis index, about $0.14 a task.
friendlySummary: Meta released Muse Ember on 9 November. It is built for the small steps an agent repeats, such as calling a tool, reading a file, or pulling a fact from a long document. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens. Meta says its best setting scores 36 on a public test, at about $0.14 a task.
whyItMatters: That is the same index score Meta cites for Claude Haiku 5.5's best setting, at a lower price on Meta's chart. It is a model for volume, not for the hardest job. If an agent spends most of its tokens on small structured steps, this is the price to compare.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Meta says that score matches the best score of a similar Claude model, at a lower price on Meta's chart. Use it when you have many small tasks. Do not assume it is the right model for the hardest job.
